videos.script: Lesson 7 deployed one artifact to two places. This lesson is about the places. {{places}} An environment is everything around the program. The port it listens on, the carrier it asks, the data it holds, and who may touch it. The program itself should be the same everywhere. {{same}} You will deploy one release of shipquote to three environments, and ask all three the same question. Two answers come back, and the difference is configuration, not code. {{answers}} Then the differences nobody chose. A time zone, a database engine, a version of Python. And one made by hand: a file edited in staging that the version number cannot see. You will watch it happen, find it with a diff, and remove it the only safe way, through the pipeline. {{drift}} After that, an environment created for a single pull request and thrown away in less than a second. {{preview}} The lesson ends with the two things that decide whether environments stay honest. What data each one holds, and who is allowed to deploy where. {{rules}}
